newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: U.S., Pakistan agree to set up business forum.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Pakistan agree to set up business forum.

text.p: The United States and Pakistan have agreed to set up a joint forum to promote business activity between the two countries, U.S. Assistant Secretary of Commerce Raymond Vickery said on Saturday.

He told a news conference after a three-day visit to Pakistan that he and Pakistani Board of Investment secretary Mohibullah Shah had signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) for setting up what will be known as the U.S.-Pakistan Business Development Forum.

The two sides will immediately proceed to implement the agreement, under which "U.S. and Pakistani businesses would work together toward the goals of promoting commercial activity and resolving issues in the commercial relationship", he said.

Vickery said that in his talks with officials from both the public and private sectors in Pakistan, he also emphasised the importance of the role of small and medium-size enterprises in bilateral commercial relationships and the role of environmental technologies, and discussed MOUs in these fields.

Further progress was made toward finalising an MOU regarding small and medium-size enterprises, which has already been under discussion, while the U.S. side gave the Pakistani government a draft MOU on using environmental technologies that is expected to be signed later this year, he said.
Vickery said he had come to "emphasise that a strong commercial relationship is in the best interests of Pakistan and the United States," and that he had succeeded.

"The Clinton administration believes that full and fair commercial interaction can be a major factor in building the prosperity, peace and stability that we wish for ourselves and for future generations," he said.
Vickery said he met officials of U.S. companies working in Pakistan, particularly to obtain their views on what should be done to strengthen the Pakistan-U.S. commercial ties.

"I paid particular attention to, and encouraged, initiatives that Pakistan has undertaken in using private sector technologies to facilitate infrastructure development in such sectors as electrical power generation, telecommunications and transportation facilities," he said.
Vickery said the U.S. Boeing Co and McDonnel Douglas Corp would be interested in helping state-run Pakistan International Airlines expand and modernise its fleet.
